title: Steerable by Design: Conditional Pretraining for Robust Control of Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.32199v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Our goal is to build language models that are steerable by design. Today's language models are pretrained with next-token prediction, which relegates alignment and control to the final 1% of training tokens or inference-time interventions. These models repurpose a single input channel for both instructions and data, leading to common failure modes where the model mistakenly treats data as instructions such as intentional jailbreaks and unintentional in-context alignment drift. To correct this, we propose a pretraining method and architecture that separates the two from the very start, producing Mancelle-3B. An encoder processes high-level semantic features of upcoming text with cross-attention that prevents the token stream from writing back into this control channel. During pretraining, the model learns to rely on these features to predict the next token, turning the channel into an effective handle for steering the model. Mancelle-3B

translated_title: 可操控性设计：用于语言模型鲁棒控制的条件预训练
translated_abstract: 我们的目标是构建在设计上就具备可操控性的语言模型。当今的语言模型采用下一词预测进行预训练，这将模型的对齐与控制推迟到训练最后1%的token或推理阶段的干预。这些模型将单一输入通道同时用于指令和数据，导致了常见的失败模式——模型错误地将数据当作指令处理，例如有意的越狱攻击和无意的上下文对齐漂移。为了解决这一问题，我们提出了一种从训练一开始就将两者分离的预训练方法和架构，由此产生了Mancelle-3B。一个编码器通过交叉注意力机制处理后续文本的高层语义特征，并阻止token流向该控制通道回写。在预训练过程中，模型学会依赖这些特征来预测下一个token，从而将该通道转变为操控模型的有效抓手。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种条件预训练方法和架构，通过编码器交叉注意力机制从一开始就将指令与数据通道分离，构建出Mancelle-3B这一在设计上即可被有效操控的语言模型，解决了模型误将数据当作指令处理的越狱与对齐漂移问题。
